primitives.name: Quarterback Decision Latency
primitives.verbatim_quote: He must remember that, when there are two or three things that can be done, it is best to do one of them confidently and without a moment's delay, even though it be the second-best choice, rather than delay and shake the team's confidence in his judgment.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \Delta t_{decision}: Time taken for quarterback to make a decision (seconds); \Delta t_{optimal}: Optimal decision time threshold (seconds)
primitives.assumptions: Assumes constant decision-making capacity and linear utility loss with delay.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \Delta t_{decision} > \Delta t_{optimal}, team confidence drops exponentially.

layer2.mapping: Maps quarterback decision latency to GSI market microstructure inefficiency, where delayed signal execution leads to adverse selection and reduced betting confidence.
layer2.telemetry: Quarterback decision time measured via game clock difference between snap and signal.

primitives.name: Center-Quarterback Alignment Protocol
primitives.verbatim_quote: The moment the ball is down, the center should be over it ready for the next play, with the quarterback behind him, always showing himself to the team as alive, sure of himself, aggressive.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: d_{align}: Distance between center and quarterback (meters); d_{align}(t_0): Initial alignment distance (meters); v_{align}: Alignment velocity (meters/second); t: Current time (seconds); t_0: Snap time (seconds)
primitives.assumptions: Assumes rigid body motion and no external interference during alignment.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Alignment fails when v_{align} \to 0 or when external noise disrupts the formation.

layer2.mapping: Maps spatial alignment to GSE state-transition logic, where precise timing and positioning ensure correct playbook execution and prevent miscommunication errors.
layer2.telemetry: Center-quarterback distance tracked via tracking data after each down.

primitives.name: Opponent Weight-Age Profiling
primitives.verbatim_quote: Preliminary to the direction of the play in the games, the quarterback should know as far as possible the weight, age, and experience of every member of the opposing team.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: W_i: Weight of opponent i (kilograms); A_j: Age of opponent j (years); E_k: Experience level of opponent k (years); K_{profiling}: Knowledge score quantifying opponent profile (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Assumes independent contribution of weight, age, and experience to predictive power.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Profiling collapses when data sparsity exceeds a threshold, leading to random play selection.

layer2.mapping: Maps profiling to GSI predictive modeling, where prior knowledge reduces uncertainty in outcome distributions and improves betting odds.
layer2.telemetry: Average weight, age, and career length of defensive players used as input features for predictive models.
